comment: Shared wire fixtures. Both the C++ codec (tests/net_test.cpp) and the VS Code client assert against these; the client keeps a vendored copy at test-fixtures/protocol_vectors.json in https://github.com/xeghosted/rage-script-manager, so a framing change has to be made in both places.
resource_name_max_comment: The longest resource name the lifecycle ops (START/STOP/RESTART/RESINFO) can carry, in bytes; their handlers decode it into a fixed buffer of this size plus a NUL. The runtime's own valid_name() enforces the SAME number, so a name the wire cannot act on is never listed as startable either -- a 183-character directory used to be advertised by RESLIST as 'stopped' while all four ops answered 'payload too long'. tests/net_test.cpp asserts net::RESOURCE_NAME_MAX against this number and tests/lua/resource_test.lua asserts valid_name's limit against it, so the two cannot drift apart.
opcodes_comment: The opcode table itself, not just its encoding. Each suite asserts every name here against its OWN language's enum constant -- net::OP_* in C++, Op.* in TypeScript -- and that it found all of them. That is what makes the two enums unable to drift: renumbering one side alone turns that side red. The vectors below pin the byte encoding on top of this; they alone never did, because both suites read their op numbers straight out of this file.
